newsitem.title: USA: SEC chief urges accountants to keep independence.
newsitem.headline: SEC chief urges accountants to keep independence.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt urged auditors on Tuesday to maintain their independence, saying it was key for the integrity of financial data issued to the marketplace.
In remarks before a conference of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, Levitt said auditors must accept certain limitations to keep their independence.

"To maintain both the fact and appearance of independence and thus the confidence of investors, auditors must avoid all suggestions of mutuality of interests with management" of companies they audit, he said.
Levitt warned, however, that the rise in consulting and other services by auditing firms has raised concerns.

He said there are "certain rumblings above the below the surface" that suggest that accounting firms may be "discounting" the importance investors place on the objectivity and independence of auditors.
"I share those concerns. The auditing function should be at the very soul of the public accounting profession, not a loss-leader retained as a foot in the door for higher-fee consulting services."

William McLucas, SEC's enforcement chief, said the issue of auditors' independence has become complicated as they now can form joint ventures with their clients and perform a host of strategic services including those involving mergers.
He said there was the possibility of bowing to pressure from clients, which he said was a threat to auditors' independence.
